items.text: Under Initiative 71 (in force since February 2015), adults 21 and over may possess and carry up to 2 ounces (about 57 g) of cannabis and give up to 1 ounce to another adult for free. Selling it outside the licensed medical system stays illegal, and using it in any public space or anywhere the public is invited, including restaurants, bars and cafes, is illegal. Initiative 71 doesn't apply on federal property, such as National Park Service land, which includes the National Mall.

Medical cannabis: domestic and international visitors may buy from any licensed DC retailer after registering online for a temporary patient registration (digital, usable straight away; non-residents self-certify that they buy to treat a health condition). Visitors 21 and over enrolled in a medical program of a listed state or territory can instead show that registration and photo ID; Virginia patients need a practitioner's written certification.

Initiative 81 (the Entheogenic Plant and Fungus Policy Act of 2020) makes non-commercial activity by adults with entheogenic plants and fungi, such as psilocybin mushrooms, ibogaine, DMT and mescaline, among the police's lowest enforcement priorities. It doesn't make them legal, and in 2025 the Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Board found it no bar to enforcement against a business.
DMT-containing plants such as those in ayahuasca are covered by the same Initiative 81 lowest-priority policy as psilocybin: lower police priority, not legal status.

laws.rule: Drivers in DC may not hold a mobile phone or other wireless device, or use one without a hands-free accessory, while driving (D.C. Code 50-1731.04). Texting or app use that causes serious injury or death carries criminal penalties.
laws.penalty_signal: US$100 fine; US$150 for a repeat within 18 months (about A$142 and A$213 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026); licence suspension after three violations in 18 months

laws.rule: Drinking alcohol or holding an open container of it is banned on streets, alleys, parks, sidewalks and parking areas, and in a vehicle on any of them (D.C. Code 25-1001). Licensed events and some home porches with the resident's permission are exceptions.
laws.penalty_signal: Misdemeanour: a fine, up to 60 days in jail, or both

laws.rule: DC requires firearms to be registered with the Metropolitan Police, and bans possessing magazines that hold more than 10 rounds. A non-resident with a firearm not registered in DC should travel straight through without stopping, with the firearm unloaded and neither it nor ammunition reachable from the passenger area (in a locked container other than the glovebox or console if there is no boot).

Adults 21 and over may possess, use, purchase or transport 2 ounces or less of marijuana (DC Code 48-904.01(a)(1)). It is unlawful to smoke or otherwise consume marijuana on a street, alley, park, sidewalk or parking area, in a vehicle on any of those, or in any place the public is invited, including private clubs (48-911.01(a)). Being impaired and endangering people or property is also banned. Cannabis stays illegal under US federal law, including on federal land in the District.
laws.penalty_signal: misdemeanour: fine under DC Code 22-3571.01 or up to 60 days in jail
